Hi Elaine — great to speak today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

- Redwood posture: SOC 2 Type II in progress (control baseline complete; auditor engaged, expected report Q3 2026). We can share the SOC 2 roadmap and interim evidence (controls matrix, penetration test summary).
- Data boundaries: Hosted API keeps customer data isolated per-tenant; option to route requests to Dedicated/Private for strict isolation. We do not use customer data to train models.
- Subprocessors: major infra providers (AWS us-west-2 for hosted, GCS for backups, S3 for model artifacts, and a managed logging partner). I attached a working subprocessor spreadsheet with hostname/role, data types touched, and encryption-at-rest details.

Action items (proposed):
1) I’ll send the redwood subprocessor list + short VSQ answers (attached).
2) If you can run the vendor security questionnaire (VSQ) and flag any blocking controls, we’ll prioritize those in the next 72 hours.
3) Markus (cc) will follow up on DPA language for HIPAA/GDPR and explicitly note KMS options.

Would you prefer the SOC 2 interim evidence or the full controls matrix first? Also, is there a preferred procurement timeline (target signature date)?

Thanks — talk soon.

--

Thanks Vanessa — useful summary. A few clarifying Qs before we run this through our security review:

1) SOC 2: when you say "in progress", can you share the auditor name and the expected date for the Type II report? We need an ETA for our compliance committee.
2) Subprocessor detail: can you confirm whether any subcontractors have access to plaintext customer prompts (e.g., logging vendors or third-party monitoring)? If so, who and under what controls?
3) HIPAA/GDPR: we have PHI in some flows. Please confirm whether Redwood will sign a full HIPAA DPA or a GDPR Data Processing Addendum with EU SCCs.

Procurement note: our target is to complete vendor security review + legal sign-off by 2026-06-01. If you can turn around the remaining docs and answers in the next week, that keeps us on track.

Also, please send the subprocessor list as a CSV (we ingest into our tooling).

Best,

Elaine — adding a note from legal/compliance side. A couple of items we will include in the DPA and the onboarding checklist:

- Encryption & keys: customers can choose Redwood-managed KMS (AES-256 at rest + customer-specific prefixes) or bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS integrations. If PHI is in-scope we will require BYOK for production environments.
- Audit evidence: we can provide SOC 2 interim artifacts (control descriptions, exception logs) and a redacted pen-test report under NDA. Full Type II report will be provided upon issuance.
- Subprocessors: any subprocessor with potential access to customer data will be listed in the CSV with role, data type touched, and contract clause references (e.g., subprocessors with access to telemetry vs. model artifacts).

Vanessa — can you confirm whether the backup bucket for model artifacts is encrypted with customer-managed keys for FinTechCorp if they choose Dedicated? If so, we should flag that in the CSV.
